resources.string: AI prediction only — not a confirmed plant disease diagnosis.
This model recognises four tomato leaf classes only. Anything else — another crop, another disease, or a non-leaf image — will still produce one of these four labels, and that output is meaningless.
The model is not confident about this image. Treat the result as unreliable.
Much of this photograph was outside the centre square the model sees. Any symptom near the edges was cropped away. Re-shoot with the leaf centred and filling the frame.

AGRI-SHIELD AI

Architecture: MobileNetV2, 4-class tomato leaf classifier
Input: 1 x 3 x 96 x 96, RGB, NCHW, float32
Runtime: ExecuTorch 1.5.1, XNNPACK backend
Execution: entirely on-device

Supported classes:
 • Tomato Early Blight
 • Tomato Late Blight
 • Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot
 • Healthy Tomato Leaf

Offline by construction: this application declares no INTERNET permission, so it cannot contact a network even if asked to.

Known limitation: the classifier was trained on laboratory photographs of detached leaves against uniform backgrounds. On real-world field images an external evaluation measured 0.3914 accuracy against 0.9562 in-domain. Predictions on field photographs should be treated with corresponding caution.

Advisory: Llama 3.2 1B Instruct (SpinQuant INT4) runs through ExecuTorch on the phone and explains the result in plain language. It is never given product names or doses. Recommended products and doses are shown separately, copied from the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) Agritech portal with the source link. When the classifier is unsure (confidence below 80% or a near-tie with another class), no product is shown at all.

Developed for the Bharat AI-SoC Challenge 2026–27.
